title: Baked French Onion Dip
summary: Caramelized onions, gruyère and crispy pancetta in a hot, bubbly dip; French onion soup you scoop.
difficulty_reason: Mostly patient stirring, then mix and bake; nothing technical.

ingredients.line: 1 1/2 cups freshly grated gruyère, plus more for topping
1 cup freshly grated mozzarella, plus more for topping
A small splash of basil (about 1/2 tsp dried)
Crostini, baguette slices or crackers, for dipping

steps: Heat the oven to 375°F. Cook the pancetta in a large pot over medium heat until it renders and turns golden and crispy.
Remove the pancetta with a slotted spoon and leave the fat in the pot.
Add the onions with a pinch of salt and a splash of water. Cover so they soften and get started.
Uncover and cook the onions slowly, stirring often, for 40 to 50 minutes, until deeply golden and jammy.
Stir in the garlic and thyme, then deglaze with the sherry and cook until it evaporates. Set the onions aside to cool a bit.
In a large bowl, mix the cream cheese, mayonnaise, sour cream, gruyère, mozzarella, black pepper and basil until smooth.
Fold in the caramelized onions and most of the pancetta.
Spread the mixture in a baking dish, then top with extra gruyère, mozzarella and the remaining pancetta.
Bake 20 to 25 minutes, until bubbly and golden on top. Serve hot with crostini or crackers.
tips: Grate the cheese yourself; pre-shredded cheese melts less smoothly.
Let the onions cook down slowly on medium-low. Rushing them gives you fried onions, not jam.
